title: Directed colimits of sheaves of commutative algebras on a ringed space
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and $\mathcal O_X$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $X$. A *sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras* is a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal A$ on $X$ together with a morphism of sheaves of rings $\sigma:\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal A$; it is an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] by $r\cdot a=\sigma(r)a$, and a morphism $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ of sheaves of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras is a morphism of sheaves of rings commuting with the structure maps. Let $I$ be a directed set and $(\mathcal A_i,\varphi_{i'i}:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A_{i'})_{i\le i'}$ a system of sheaves of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras ($\varphi_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, $\varphi_{i''i'}\varphi_{i'i}=\varphi_{i''i}$). Let $\mathcal P$ be the presheaf $U\mapsto\varinjlim_i\mathcal A_i(U)$ (directed colimit of commutative rings, with the restriction maps induced by those of the $\mathcal A_i$ and with the coprojections $c_{i,U}:\mathcal A_i(U)\to\mathcal P(U)$), a presheaf of commutative rings with the map $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal P$, $r\mapsto c_{i,U}(\sigma_i(r))$ (independent of $i$). Let $\theta:\mathcal P\to\mathcal A:=\mathcal P^\#$ be its sheafification as a presheaf of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and $\iota_i=\theta\circ c_i:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A$. Then: (1) $\mathcal A$ with $\sigma=\theta\circ(\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal P)$ is a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras, the $\iota_i$ are morphisms of such with $\iota_{i'}\varphi_{i'i}=\iota_i$, and $(\mathcal A,(\iota_i))$ is a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of the system in the category of sheaves of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras; (2) the underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module of $\mathcal A$, with the $\iota_i$, is a colimit of the underlying $\mathcal O_X$-modules of the $\mathcal A_i$ in the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules.

source.place: Sheaves, Section 009D (section-limits-presheaves: colimits of presheaves are sectionwise), Section 009E (section-limits-sheaves, item (3): the colimit of sheaves is the sheafification of the presheaf colimit), Lemma 0087 (lemma-sheafify-presheaf-structures: sheafification of a presheaf of algebraic structures, (1) underlying sheaf of sets, (2) universal property), Lemma 0089 (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules); Modules, Lemma 01AH (modules.tex, lemma-limits-colimits, (2): colimits in Mod(O_X) are the sheafification of the presheaf colimit). The assembly for algebras over O_X is not stated in Stacks as one lemma (it is used in Schemes, Section 26.24, and Limits 01YX).

proof.text: *Step 1 (the presheaf colimit $\mathcal P$ is a presheaf of commutative rings under $\mathcal O_X$).* $I$ is nonempty (a directed set is nonempty, Stacks Categories, Definition 00D3) and, regarded as a category ($i\to i'$ iff $i\le i'$), filtered. Fix an open $U\subseteq X$ and put $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$. Each $\mathcal A_i(U)$ is a commutative $R$-algebra by $\sigma_{i,U}$, and the $\varphi_{i'i,U}$ are $R$-algebra maps (they commute with the structure maps). By [lem-weil-pbc-commutative-algebras-colimits-exist] the system $(\mathcal A_i(U),\varphi_{i'i,U})$ has a colimit $(\mathcal P(U),(c_{i,U}))$ in commutative $R$-algebras, with structure map $\sigma_{\mathcal P,U}:R\to\mathcal P(U)$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise](1) $(\mathcal P(U),(c_{i,U}))$ is also a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of the underlying system of commutative rings; this is the directed colimit of the statement (any other choice is uniquely isomorphic to it compatibly with the coprojections). Since $c_{i,U}$ is an $R$-algebra map, $c_{i,U}\circ\sigma_{i,U}=\sigma_{\mathcal P,U}$ for every $i$: the map $r\mapsto c_{i,U}(\sigma_{i,U}(r))$ is independent of $i$. For opens $V\subseteq U$ the ring maps $c_{i,V}\circ\mathrm{res}^{\mathcal A_i}_{U,V}:\mathcal A_i(U)\to\mathcal P(V)$ satisfy $c_{i',V}\,\mathrm{res}\,\varphi_{i'i,U}=c_{i',V}\varphi_{i'i,V}\,\mathrm{res}=c_{i,V}\,\mathrm{res}$ (the $\varphi_{i'i}$ are morphisms of presheaves), so by the universal property of the ring colimit there is exactly one ring map $\rho_{U,V}:\mathcal P(U)\to\mathcal P(V)$ with $\rho_{U,V}c_{i,U}=c_{i,V}\,\mathrm{res}_{U,V}$ for all $i$. Uniqueness gives $\rho_{U,U}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\rho_{V,W}\rho_{U,V}=\rho_{U,W}$ for $W\subseteq V\subseteq U$ (both sides satisfy the defining identity), so $\mathcal P$ is a presheaf of commutative rings and the $c_i:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal P$ are morphisms of presheaves of rings with $c_{i'}\varphi_{i'i}=c_i$. Finally $\sigma_{\mathcal P}$ is a morphism of presheaves of rings $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal P$: $\rho_{U,V}\sigma_{\mathcal P,U}(r)=\rho_{U,V}c_{i,U}\sigma_{i,U}(r)=c_{i,V}(\sigma_{i,U}(r)|_V)=c_{i,V}\sigma_{i,V}(r|_V)=\sigma_{\mathcal P,V}(r|_V)$, since $\sigma_i$ is a morphism of sheaves.

source.place: Sheaves, Section 009D (section-limits-presheaves: colimits of presheaves are computed sectionwise, $(\colim_i\mathcal F_i)(U)=\colim_i\mathcal F_i(U)$, 'the proofs are all easy'); written out here for presheaves of rings under $\mathcal O_X$, with Algebra, Lemma 00D6 for the directed colimit

proof.text: *Step 2 (the underlying presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules of $\mathcal P$ is the colimit in presheaves of modules).* Regard $\mathcal A_i$ and $\mathcal P$ as presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] by $r\cdot a=\sigma_i(r)a$ and $r\cdot p=\sigma_{\mathcal P}(r)p$; the restriction maps are semilinear because $\sigma_i,\sigma_{\mathcal P}$ commute with restriction and the restrictions are ring maps (Step 1), and $\varphi_{i'i}$, $c_i$ are $\mathcal O_X$-linear because they are ring maps commuting with the structure maps. Claim: for each open $U$, $(\mathcal P(U),(c_{i,U}))$ is a colimit of the $R$-modules $\mathcal A_i(U)$, $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$. Let $g_i:\mathcal A_i(U)\to M$ be $R$-linear with $g_{i'}\varphi_{i'i,U}=g_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise](2) every element of $\mathcal P(U)$ is $c_{i,U}(a)$ for some $i$ and $a\in\mathcal A_i(U)$; put $g(c_{i,U}(a))=g_i(a)$. This is well defined: if $c_{i,U}(a)=c_{j,U}(b)$ then by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-rings-zero] there is $k\ge i,j$ with $\varphi_{ki}(a)=\varphi_{kj}(b)$, so $g_i(a)=g_k\varphi_{ki}(a)=g_k\varphi_{kj}(b)=g_j(b)$. It is additive: two elements can be written $c_{k,U}(a),c_{k,U}(b)$ at a common index $k$ ($I$ directed, $c_{k}\varphi_{ki}=c_i$), and $c_{k,U}(a)+c_{k,U}(b)=c_{k,U}(a+b)$. It is $R$-linear: $r\cdot c_{i,U}(a)=\sigma_{\mathcal P}(r)c_{i,U}(a)=c_{i,U}(\sigma_i(r))c_{i,U}(a)=c_{i,U}(r\cdot a)$, so $g(r\cdot c_{i,U}(a))=g_i(ra)=rg_i(a)$. Clearly $gc_{i,U}=g_i$, and $g$ is unique with this property because the images of the $c_{i,U}$ cover $\mathcal P(U)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-modules-colimits-sectionwise] the sectionwise colimit $\mathcal Q:V\mapsto\colim_i\mathcal A_i(V)$ (colimit of $\mathcal O_X(V)$-modules) with its coprojections $q_i$ is a colimit of the diagram $(\mathcal A_i)$ in the category $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O_X)$ of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. By the claim, for each $U$ there is a unique $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear isomorphism $\alpha_U:\mathcal Q(U)\to\mathcal P(U)$ with $\alpha_Uq_{i,U}=c_{i,U}$ (comparison of two colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]); $\alpha$ commutes with restrictions, since $\rho_{U,V}\alpha_U$ and $\alpha_V\,\mathrm{res}^{\mathcal Q}_{U,V}$ agree on every $q_{i,U}(a)$ and maps out of $\mathcal Q(U)$ are determined by their composites with the $q_{i,U}$. So $\alpha:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal P$ is an isomorphism in $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O_X)$ carrying $q_i$ to $c_i$, and $(\mathcal P,(c_i))$ is a colimit of $(\mathcal A_i)$ in $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O_X)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit: the directed colimit of modules as $\coprod M_i/\sim$ with operations at a common later index; the same set and addition underlie the directed colimit of rings) and Lemma 00D7 (lemma-zero-directed-limit); Sheaves, Section 009D (sheaves.tex, colimits of presheaves sectionwise); Modules, Lemma 01AH (modules.tex, lemma-limits-colimits) for presheaves of modules

proof.text: *Step 3 (the sheafification is a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-algebras and the $\iota_i$ form a cocone; first half of (1)).* By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheafification-space-underlying-abelian](1) the presheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal P$ of Step 1 has a sheafification $\theta:\mathcal P\to\mathcal A=\mathcal P^\#$ in sheaves of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Put $\sigma=\theta\circ\sigma_{\mathcal P}:\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal A$, a composite of morphisms of presheaves of rings between sheaves, hence a morphism of sheaves of rings; so $(\mathcal A,\sigma)$ is a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras, an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] by $r\cdot a=\sigma(r)a$ (restriction is semilinear since $\sigma$ and the restrictions of $\mathcal A$ are ring maps compatible with restriction). The maps $\iota_i=\theta\circ c_i$ are morphisms of sheaves of rings with $\iota_i\sigma_i=\theta c_i\sigma_i=\theta\sigma_{\mathcal P}=\sigma$ (Step 1), i.e. morphisms of sheaves of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras, and $\iota_{i'}\varphi_{i'i}=\theta c_{i'}\varphi_{i'i}=\theta c_i=\iota_i$. Moreover $\theta$ is $\mathcal O_X$-linear from the presheaf of modules $\mathcal P$ of Step 2 to $\mathcal A$: $\theta(\sigma_{\mathcal P}(r)p)=\theta(\sigma_{\mathcal P}(r))\theta(p)=\sigma(r)\theta(p)$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 0087 (lemma-sheafify-presheaf-structures) for commutative rings; Section 009E (section-limits-sheaves) item (3): the colimit is the sheafification of the presheaf colimit

proof.text: *Step 4 (universal property in sheaves of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras; rest of (1)).* Let $(\mathcal B,\tau)$ be a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras and $\beta_i:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal B$ morphisms of such with $\beta_{i'}\varphi_{i'i}=\beta_i$. For each open $U$ the ring maps $\beta_{i,U}$ are compatible with the $\varphi_{i'i,U}$, so by the colimit property of $(\mathcal P(U),(c_{i,U}))$ in rings (Step 1, [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]) there is exactly one ring map $b_U:\mathcal P(U)\to\mathcal B(U)$ with $b_Uc_{i,U}=\beta_{i,U}$ for all $i$. The family $b$ is a morphism of presheaves: $\mathrm{res}^{\mathcal B}_{U,V}b_U$ and $b_V\rho_{U,V}$ are ring maps $\mathcal P(U)\to\mathcal B(V)$ whose composites with $c_{i,U}$ both equal $\beta_{i,V}\,\mathrm{res}_{U,V}$ ($\beta_i$ commutes with restriction), so they are equal by uniqueness. And $b\sigma_{\mathcal P}=bc_i\sigma_i=\beta_i\sigma_i=\tau$. By the universal property of $\theta$ ([lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheafification-space-underlying-abelian](1)) there is exactly one morphism of sheaves of commutative rings $u:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ with $u\theta=b$. Then $u\iota_i=u\theta c_i=bc_i=\beta_i$ and $u\sigma=u\theta\sigma_{\mathcal P}=b\sigma_{\mathcal P}=\tau$, so $u$ is a morphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-algebras with $u\iota_i=\beta_i$. Uniqueness: if $u'$ is a morphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-algebras with $u'\iota_i=\beta_i$ for all $i$, then $(u'\theta)_Uc_{i,U}=\beta_{i,U}$ for all $i,U$, so $u'\theta=b$ by the uniqueness of each $b_U$, hence $u'=u$ by the uniqueness in the universal property of $\theta$. So $(\mathcal A,(\iota_i))$ is a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of the system in sheaves of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras.

source.place: Sheaves, Section 009E (section-limits-sheaves) item (3) and Lemma 0087 (2) (universal property of the sheafification of a presheaf of algebraic structures); the assembly for algebras under $\mathcal O_X$ is not stated in Stacks and is written out here

proof.text: *Step 5 (the underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module is the colimit in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$; clause (2)).* Let $\eta:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P^\#_{\mathrm{mod}}$ be the sheafification of the presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal P$ of Step 2 [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] (on the opens of $X$, abelian presheaves have sheafifications: Stacks Sheaves, Lemma 0085, [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]); it is left adjoint to the inclusion $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O_X)$. (a) *$\mathcal P^\#_{\mathrm{mod}}$ with the $\eta c_i$ is a colimit of $(\mathcal A_i)$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$.* By Step 2, $(\mathcal P,(c_i))$ is a colimit of the $\mathcal A_i$ in $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O_X)$; by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] the sheafification sends it to a colimit $(\mathcal P^\#_{\mathrm{mod}},(c_i^\#))$ of the $\mathcal A_i^\#$, where $c_i^\#\eta_{\mathcal A_i}=\eta c_i$. Since $\mathcal A_i$ is already a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, $\eta_{\mathcal A_i}:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A_i^\#$ is an isomorphism (the identity of $\mathcal A_i$ factors as $e\eta_{\mathcal A_i}$, and $\eta_{\mathcal A_i}e\eta_{\mathcal A_i}=\eta_{\mathcal A_i}$ gives $\eta_{\mathcal A_i}e=\mathrm{id}$ by uniqueness of factorizations), natural in $i$; replacing $\mathcal A_i^\#$ by $\mathcal A_i$ along these isomorphisms, $(\mathcal P^\#_{\mathrm{mod}},(\eta c_i))$ is a colimit of $(\mathcal A_i)$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. (b) *Comparison with $\mathcal A$.* By Step 3, $\theta:\mathcal P\to\mathcal A$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map into a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so $\theta=v\eta$ for exactly one $\mathcal O_X$-linear $v:\mathcal P^\#_{\mathrm{mod}}\to\mathcal A$. Forget the module structures: the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal P^\#_{\mathrm{mod}}$ with $\eta$ is the sheafification of the underlying abelian presheaf of $\mathcal P$ (by the construction in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]), and so is the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal A$ with $\theta$ ([lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheafification-space-underlying-abelian](2)). By the universal property of $\theta$ among abelian sheaves there is a morphism of abelian sheaves $w:\mathcal A\to\mathcal P^\#_{\mathrm{mod}}$ with $w\theta=\eta$; then $wv\eta=\eta$ and $vw\theta=\theta$, so $wv=\mathrm{id}$ and $vw=\mathrm{id}$ by the uniqueness parts of the two universal properties [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Hence $v$ is bijective on every open; the inverse of an $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear bijection is linear, so $v$ is an isomorphism in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, and $v\eta c_i=\theta c_i=\iota_i$. Transporting (a) along $v$: the underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module of $\mathcal A$, with the $\iota_i$, is a colimit of the underlying $\mathcal O_X$-modules of the $\mathcal A_i$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$.
